Fix exactly the two review findings below, and nothing beside them.
- Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED.
- Decision 0091 is ACCEPTED. The operator ruled "accept all for 0090" on PR #793 on 2026-10-20. That is 0091, renumbered with its text unchanged. It is recorded on #717 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/717#issuecomment-6284444153).
- The choices 0091 left open were ruled before the story ran. On 2026-10-21 the operator said, verbatim: "accept all for 717 slice 3b". It is recorded on #717 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/717#issuecomment-6312710732). TAKE 4, quoted: "the order word, 4, 5, 1, 3, 2, with a closed-word text of your writing in the house's form".
- Read decision 0091 ruling 1 (:156-216) before you start.

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH (your diff is judged against 09b4fe86):
- 4dba42a9: the story run, rebased onto main afc97d1f. Its review stopped on a security hold.
- 3654d4e4, 1c432ffe and 09b4fe86: fix round 717s3b2, run fix-round-717s3b2-for-story-717--87cb4d46. It fixed the hold's three findings. The folder side's `from` is read by the one word reading. In a folder, the recipe's own driver is held to what a compile with no folder runs, by `assemble::hold_own_drivers` running `compile_seat` on a scratch compiler (assemble.rs:130, called at bundle.rs:1009). And the hands-less folder seat is bound.
- That round's review verified all three as fixed, then parked with two MEDIUMs after two reforgings (REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM). Neither is a security residual, and every input is still refused. The run stays parked; this round is its successor.
- When you are done, the branch is 09b4fe86 plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main.

THE FINDINGS (the review chief's, reproduced with target/debug/brokkr). For each, write an exact test and record a removal control: undo the fix in a scratch edit, see the test fail with its stated text, then restore. Keep a copy set aside and restore with cp. git stash is shared across worktrees: never stash.

1. MEDIUM. In a composed child, refusal 4 loses its variant and gains a second prefix.
   - Where: the chain-note wrap in `Bundle::compile_as` (bundle.rs, about :934-943). `hold_own_drivers` raises refusal 4 inside `assemble`, and the catch-all arm `(Some(note), error) => CompileError::Invalid(format!("{error} ({note})"))` re-wraps it.
   - Reproduced: a child `{"name":"child","extends":"fixture"}` over a fixture whose verify says "from": "folder" with driver null, and a valid folder. It printed exactly:
     `error: bundle: bundle: seat verify says "from": "folder" and declares no driver of its own, which a compile with no folder runs (decision 0091) (composed: child -> fixture)`
     The same child with the driver ABSENT prints refusal 4 once, unwrapped, because the resolver raises it before the note wraps (bundle.rs, about :929).
   - So the inherited case loses `CompileError::Folder(FolderSeatRefusal::NoOwnDriver)`. That breaks decision 0071 ruling 8 (match the variant) and the last round's commission ("refusal 4's existing variant and exact text").
   - The fix: a `CompileError::Folder` refusal passes through the chain wrap with its variant and its text unchanged, exactly as the resolver's folder refusals already rise. Every other variant's wrapping stays byte-identical: Capability, Policy (ComposedPolicy) and the Invalid catch-all.
     - Read every `CompileError::Folder` raise site first. If any of them can reach the wrap today with a text that relies on the chain note, say so in your notes and stop.
   - Bind it: the composed child over the null-driver fixture refuses with `CompileError::Folder(FolderSeatRefusal::NoOwnDriver { seat: "verify" })` (match the variant) and refusal 4's exact single text. That is the same as the absent-driver child. Add a test or a reading that an Invalid refusal from a composed child still carries its "(composed: …)" note, so the other arms are held.

2. MEDIUM. Refusal 4's precedence holds only for an ABSENT driver.
   - Where: folder.rs `from()` (about :310-320) tests key presence in the resolver, so an absent driver refuses at TAKE 4's place. A PRESENT driver that the no-folder compile would refuse (null, {} or {"command": []}) is caught only by `hold_own_drivers`. That runs in `assemble`, after `resolve_unsealed`, so the resolver's refusals 5, 1, 3 and 2 come first. Reproduced: driver null with a folder declaring no verify gives refusal 1; with the folder command ["echo","hello"], refusal 3; with the folder's results reversed, refusal 2.
   - `take()`'s doc (folder.rs, about :243-245) states one order for every case, which the code holds only for the absent case. No test binds a combined fault: every case in folder/tests.rs uses a valid folder.
   - The structural fix (holding a present driver at refusal 4's place) needs the compile's boundary, adapters, engine and machine inside the resolver. That is the operator's call, and it is asked on the PR. This round takes the RECOMMENDED path, which changes no refusal and no order:
     - Correct `take()`'s doc so it states exactly what the code does. The ruled order holds for the decision's own case, a seat that declares no driver. A seat whose driver is present but which a compile with no folder would not run is refused as refusal 4 after the resolver's refusals (5, 1, 3, 2), once the seats are compiled. Put the same sentence on `hold_own_drivers`. Do not change `from()`, `supply()` or `hold_own_drivers`' logic.
     - Bind the combined faults with exact variant and exact text, in the order the code holds:
       - present invalid driver (null) with an undeclared folder seat: refusal 1;
       - present invalid driver with a folder command that is not its own script: refusal 3;
       - present invalid driver with a differing shape: refusal 2;
       - present invalid driver with a valid folder: refusal 4;
       - ABSENT driver with an undeclared folder seat: refusal 4 (the ruled precedence);
       - present invalid driver in a composed child: refusal 4, by finding 1's fix.
     - Removal control: swap the order of two of the resolver's refusals in a scratch edit, and see the combined-fault test fail with the other refusal's text.
   - Do NOT move `compile_seat`'s context into the resolver, and do not restructure the resolver or `assemble`. If you find a way to hold a present driver at refusal 4's place without either, do not build it: describe it in your notes, and the PR will put it to the operator.

CARRIED TO THE PR, NOT THIS ROUND (do not touch):
- `hold_own_drivers` drops `compile_seat`'s cause. So an operator sees refusal 4 for, say, an unknown driver key, and learns why only by compiling with no folder. The last round's "add no new text" rules it out; it is an operator ask.
- INFO: FOLDER_PREFIX is pub(crate) with consumers only in its module. shelved() reads outside read_layer's collision check (compose/layers.rs:54). brokkr-view graph/figures.rs counts only @compose/ as base drift.

For the implement phase: fix, then run all of these clean, from the worktree root:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked (timeout 590)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked -- witness_digests:: (no re-pin: no recipe changes)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- portable_recipes:: recipes:: shelf:: brokkr_folder:: folder_seats:: decisions_index:: doc_truth:: (timeout 590)
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api
- `cargo crap --path crates/brokkr-runtime/src --format json`: every function you change or add at CC 15 or under (each `?` counts +1)
- git diff --check
- The exact-coverage gate is the controller's. Keep every new line and branch reached by a test.

The flakes tracked as #743 and #811 are not this branch's: brokkr-cli's capability_broker::handoff tests, and brokkr-runtime's engine::broker::admission tests ("Identity(Expired)" under host load). If one fails, rerun it alone once and report both runs with their whole failure text.

RULES
- Scope: these two findings and nothing beside them. Follow-ups go in your notes, not the diff.
- Tests assert exact values, exact variants and exact error text, never is_err() alone.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063).
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#717)" in the repository's style, naming each removal control, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- The implement phase alone changes files and commits. Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, and it re-runs no removal control by editing tracked files. Use a scratch copy outside the worktree.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed.
- If a fix needs new refusal text, a new key, a changed order or a change to a ruled TAKE, stop and say so in your notes. That is a new ask for the operator, not this round's to decide.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

One commit, 369754f2, on 09b4fe86. Signed off. Not pushed.

FINDING 1 (fixed). In Bundle::compile_as (bundle.rs:943) a CompileError::Folder now passes the chain-note wrap unchanged: new arm `(_, error @ CompileError::Folder(_)) | (None, error) => error`, placed before the Invalid catch-all. The Capability, ComposedPolicy and Invalid arms are byte-identical. Raise-site audit (grep for CompileError::Folder and FolderSeatRefusal::): every raise in compose/folder.rs runs inside resolve_unsealed, which returns with `?` at bundle.rs:929, before the wrap. The only raise inside assemble is assemble.rs:150 (hold_own_drivers), and its text does not depend on the chain note. Nothing relied on the note, so I went ahead. Test in_a_composed_child_refusal_four_rises_unwrapped_and_others_carry_the_note uses a child {name: child, extends: fixture} on the personal shelf. For an absent driver and for a null driver alike it gets (NoOwnDriver{seat:verify}, refusal 4's single text). A composed child with an Invalid refusal (no from, null driver) still gives Invalid("bundle: seat 'verify' missing 'role' (composed: child -> fixture)").

FINDING 2 (recommended path; no change to any refusal, text or order). take()'s doc (folder.rs:243-249) and hold_own_drivers' doc (assemble.rs:129-133) now say: the ruled order holds refusal 4 at its place for a seat that declares no driver. A present driver that a compile with no folder would not run is refused as refusal 4 after the resolver's refusals (5, 1, 3, 2), once the seats are compiled. from(), supply() and hold_own_drivers' logic are unchanged. Test refusal_four_follows_the_folders_refusals_unless_no_driver_is_declared checks exact variant and text for five cases: present null driver + undeclared folder seat -> refusal 1; + folder command that is a raw process -> refusal 3; + reversed results -> refusal 2; + sound folder -> refusal 4; absent driver + undeclared folder seat -> refusal 4. The sixth case, a present null driver in a composed child -> refusal 4, is in finding 1's test. Refusals 1, 2 and 3's texts are now pinned once (undeclared_text(), NOT_ITS_OWN_SCRIPT, DIFFERS) and shared with their existing tests, which follows the module doc's 'each pinned once' and also clears a jscpd clone that the first draft introduced.

REMOVAL CONTROLS (each a scratch edit, restored by cp from .forge/scratch/*.fixed; I re-ran all of them against the final tests):
- A: removed the Folder arm. in_a_composed_child_... FAILED with 'not a folder seat refusal: bundle: bundle: seat 'verify' says "from": "folder" and declares no driver of its own, which a compile with no folder runs (decision 0091) (composed: child -> fixture)', exactly the reproduced text.
- A2: arm `(_, error) => error` (nothing wrapped). The same test FAILED with left "seat 'verify' missing 'role'" vs right "bundle: seat 'verify' missing 'role' (composed: child -> fixture)".
